name: May Green
lede: May Green is a mid, slightly yellowish green, the name RAL gave to its standard color 6017, and one that a pigment reference files as a rare variant name for emerald green.

sections.title: A name with two uses
sections.body:
The library dates May Green to 1927, as RAL color 6017, an industrial standard color [1]. Its screen value here, #4C9141, is an approximation, and the RAL swatch sits slightly darker, at #468641 [1]. The nearest ISCC-NBS category is strong yellowish green, about 3.5 units away [1].

A second use is older and rarer. The *Pigment Compendium* lists May green among the less common names for emerald green, citing Fiedler and Bayard (1997), and suggests the term probably marks a shade variant [2]. The word *May* is never explained there, and no color book we hold says why the name was chosen [3]. Its closest relatives are [[kelly-green]], [[grass]] and [[leaf-green]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: May Green appears in 10 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.04%, as photographed [5]. It is rarer than 70% of the named colors [5]. It peaks in paintings of the 1800s, in 5 of 8,345 (0.1%), 1.4 times the rate expected from the same museums [5]. The earliest match is from 1860, 67 years before the RAL record, so it is a look-alike hue and not evidence of the pigment [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [5].
